featured_reviews.review_text: I have visited this place twice till now one on a weekday and once on a Saturday. This place has an amazing choice of food stuff, like dry fruits, hot snacks, Namkeen , Mithais, different sauces, chocolate, different types of cheese, etc. the staff here was amazingly polite and helpful. They gave us a tour of the place and were helpful in finding the product we wanted and also gave suggestions as to what their special foods were. They have parking space available outside the store for 2 to 3 four wheeler and 10 to 15 two wheeler. One must try their Mango barfi in mithai it was just amazing. They have around 7 to 8 branches all around Mumbai but this one is one of their biggest stores. We had even tried out their cheese balls and their pizza samosa which was finger liking good. One could feel that the stuff is a little bit on a higher side of cost but when compared with the quality provided it's worth every penny. They even have a lot of options for people looking for Jain and diet.

featured_reviews.review_text: I worked with Nicole to create personalized mithai boxes for my wedding announcement, and the entire experience was exceptional. featured_reviews.name: Suhasini Sudan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Love their ambience, their decorations, and their trial sweet and savoury snacks. Love their unique twist on fusion Indo-western desserts and snacks. Their Avo Papdi chaat is delicious and so are their Gulab Jamun churros, their Rasgulla Tiramisu and their special strawberry menu. Their thick hot chocolate with the special cookie is also a personal favourite. I also love their chocolate barks, especially the strawberry chocolate one.

Has become such a stable, me and my friends go there practically every week. Amazing for a treat.

featured_reviews.name: Akarsh Kavuttan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally had the opportunity to visit the famous Bombay Sweet Shop!

Although I couldn’t have much as I had already ordered a bunch of sweets earlier on the occasion of Women’s Day!

Nevertheless the vibe was fantastic! The interiors were also fantastic!

featured_reviews.name: Priya pokhare
featured_reviews.review_text: Mithais are more than just good packaging and presentation. People may be all impressed with BSS but honestly I was a bit underwhelmed. I have gifted friends and family with their items . But they are overdoing the fusion stuff , which I guess is the point but they are losing their vision. I also think they do not use good quality chocolate for their brittle and fudge. The fudge tastes flat and nothing of chocolate. The only decent thing maybe the chocolate butter cookies . I would like to like them but they need to make it make sense for the price I pay .

featured_reviews.name: Anasuya Roshan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had these delivered in Mumbai and brought over to Malaysia within 24hrs. They lasted the entire journey intact and lip smacking good!

I strongly recommend the Cheat Box, Assorted Mithai Box and Kalakand (any flavour of the Kalakand if you can get your hands on some). Bite-sized portions, provided you exercise control, which is impossible I'd say. Their namkeens are addictive, those should come with warning labels. All edibles are have allergens labelled on their packaging; it simplifies matters for those who have restrictive diets.

None of the sweets are overly sweet despite being 'sweets'. I'm not sure how to explain the irony of that sentence, but those who have an indulgent sweet tooth AND a hawk's eye on their calorie intake, you know what I mean.

Always a good experience shopping from you!

featured_reviews.name: Sassinator
featured_reviews.review_text: BSS is extraordinary!! We were introduced to the store thru an equally amazing 5 Senses Tour. We HAD to go back!! The service and the sweets were OFF THE CHARTS!! We even brought our Uber driver in to treat him to their delicious ice cream!!

featured_reviews.name: Amruta S
featured_reviews.review_text: Don’t buy from them online! I placed an online order in time for Diwali. The order was well Packaged but had an important missing item - the kaju katli burfi. Their customer service does not exist! Neither on WhatsApp, email or phone. Best to go to the store and get what you pay for instead of paying for missed items and chasing them with no result.

featured_reviews.name: Kalpesh Kandalgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai Ladu Samrat is a very popular and iconic spot in Lalbaug for authentic Maharashtrian snacks and breakfast items. The place is especially famous for its vada pav, misal pav, sabudana vada, and kothimbir vadi, all known for their strong traditional taste and quality.

The food is pocket-friendly and delicious, with soft pav and well-balanced spices. Many visitors love the quick service and consistency in taste, making it a favorite among locals.
The ambiance is simple and a bit crowded, especially during peak hours. Seating is limited, so you might have to wait or prefer takeaway. Despite that, the taste and authenticity make it worth visiting.
It’s also known as a legendary vada pav place in Mumbai, attracting heavy crowds from early morning.

featured_reviews.name: Avdesh Rana
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ladu Samrat is one of those classic Mumbai joints that has managed to keep its charm for years. If you’re a fan of Maharashtrian food, this place will definitely win you over. Their misal pav is easily the star of the menu—spicy, flavorful, and served just the way it should be. It has the perfect balance of spice and crunch, and it’s honestly one of the best I’ve had in the city. Alongside, their puran poli and modaks are must-tries if you have a sweet tooth. The flavors taste authentic and homely, like something straight out of a traditional Maharashtrian kitchen.

The restaurant itself is simple, clean, and always buzzing with people, which also means you might have to wait during peak hours. Service is quick and efficient despite the crowd, and the staff is polite. Prices are quite reasonable for Mumbai standards, and the portion sizes are filling. Don’t expect a fancy ambience—it’s more of a no-frills eatery focused on great food.

Overall, Ladu Samrat is a place you visit for its taste and authenticity, not for luxury. If you’re in Mumbai and want to experience genuine Maharashtrian flavors, this restaurant should definitely be on your list.

featured_reviews.review_text: We've been to Bombay sweet shop multiple times since their opening at phoenix palladium mall and always leave happy & content from their outlet. We had tried their gulab jamun Churros, chilli cheese toast pav bhaji porter rolls, arbi tuk chat, OG pind chole bhature,rajma galouti wrap, bhutte ka khees served with khakhra, avo papdi chat, cappuccino,hot chocolate, raspberry matcha falooda, strawberry granola sundae, jalebi waffle, strawberry softserve and caramel icecream so far. Their salted caramel icecream served with their chocolate caramel barks is a must try. Personally found churros,hot chocolate to be too sweet for my liking. You sit.
You snack.
You stay longer.

In a world full of cupcakes be a laddo.
